title: Sheinbaum Stresses Separating Economic and Political Power After Paraguayan President’s Banking Scandal
author: Alma E. Muñoz and Arturo Sánchez
content:
_This article by Alma E. Muñoz and Arturo Sánchez originally appeared in
the[November 6, 2026 edition of La
Jornada](https://www.jornada.com.mx/noticia/2026/11/06/politica/tras-
escandalo-bancario-en-paraguay-sheinbaum-sostiene-la-importancia-de-separar-
el-poder-politico-del-economico), Mexico's premier left wing daily newspaper._

**Mexico City**. In response to the banking scandal in which the former
president of Paraguay, Santiago Peña, finds himself, President Claudia
Sheinbaum Pardo highlighted the importance of **separating political power
from economic power**.

"Each one is separate," she maintained, noting that she will wait to have more
information before giving her opinion. The right-wing Santiago Peña resigned
yesterday after the banking collapse in that country and an imminent
impeachment trial against him.

"But it does seem that the now former president was involved in this bank, and
that is the reason why he made the decision to resign," President Sheinbaum
affirmed.

Yesterday, Paraguayan President Peña announced that he was leaving the
presidency after the intervention of the Ueno bank, a digital financial
institution with which he had ties, which managed **some 850 million dollars
in public funds** and whose closure left **three million customers without
access to their accounts**.

However, that country's Congress **rejected the resignation and will put him
on trial**.
